newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy shares end at day's high, unphased by EMU row.
newsitem.headline: Italy shares end at day's high, unphased by EMU row.

text.p: Italian stocks extended gains to close at the day's highs on Wednesday, boosted by a firmer Wall Street in a market expecting good figures on investment fund inflows on Thursday and unmoved by the row over the timing of Italy's entry into the single European currency, traders said.
"There's no shortage of liquidity in the market and basically on the Italy/EMU question there's nothing really fundamentally new," one dealer said.
The All-share Mibtel index closed up 1.81 percent at a session high of 12,636 and the Mib30 blue chip index ended 2.05 percent higher at an 18,827 peak.
The market had got off to a positive start after Tuesday night's government-brokered accord between metalworkers and employers putting an end to a long-standing pay dispute.

Operators said they were expecting to see sharply higher equity fund inflows in January when the investment fund data are released on Thursday morning. December saw equity inflows for the first time in many months of 369 billion lire, signalling a switch by investors out of bonds into the stock market.
Trade was seen up on Tuesday at some 1.5 trillion lire.
ENI, Banca Commerciale Italiana (BCI), Telecom Italia and Gemina were all leading performers.
In banks, BCI ended 6.42 percent higher at 3,563 lire, Mediobanca put on 3.81 percent to 11,330 and Ambroveneto rose 2.65 percent to 4,797 lire.
Energy group ENI, somewhat neglected in recent sessions, saw renewed buying orders and ended 3.41 percent up at 9,216. Fiat put on 1.36 percent to 5,421 lire.
Financial holding Gemina rose 4.45 percent to 1,034 and Olivetti gained 1.21 percent to 676.2.
In telecoms, Telecom Italia rose 4.06 percent to 4,695 lire while its holding company Stet, into which the telephone company is to be merged, put on a modest 1.43 percent to 7,998 lire.
